Related spirit-concealment spell, but it veils a caster with spirits rather than supplying an identified masked spirit entity.
The monster has an actual tentacle attack with Improved Grab, directly answering grabbing tentacles.
Useful indirect memory-erasing caster: Ziradini has innate Rewrite Memory, allowing erasure on a failed Will save within its stated memory limits.
Directly paralyzes an enemy and freezes it in place.
The spell directly paralyzes an enemy on a failed save.
Lets a creature with a fly Speed slow a fall and avoid damage on success, a useful qualified safe-descent method.
Related undead healing recipient and self temporary-HP gain, but full entries provide no undead-restoring effect: Absorb Phantom Brain grants temporary HP only to itself.
An undead recipient of void healing and personal temporary HP is related, but not a useful method to heal undead; phantom absorption grants temporary HP rather than healing.
The spell conceals someone from allies including hearing, related to silence but without any alarm mechanism.
Actual character healer has linked innate Heal uses for willing living allies.
Ordinary armor is neither a monster nor disguised monstrous treasure.
This is ordinary Hellknight armor, with no monster or disguised treasure capability.
Direct collapsing-floor hazard as adjacent rotten boards give way into a pit.
Zoog has at-will personal animal speech, useful indirect creature context rather than granting the requester speech.
Weakness-exploiting fear spell supplies no alarm or silent notification; secret terminology is coincidental.
Enfeebling wand causes contagious frailty and has no shelter-conjuring function.
Creates a luminous damaging wall, not passage through existing walls.
An arcane prepared caster with a spellbook and actual prepared Ignition is a direct wizard-with-fire-magic answer; the query does not require fire specialization.
A prepared arcane caster with usable Ignition is a qualified wizard-with-fire-magic answer; its main role is law enforcement and its fire capability is a cantrip.
Innate Dive and Breach offers qualified teleportation between nearby surfaces.
Useful indirect source of a silent alarm: Kemnebi has Alarm prepared, whose mental alert option satisfies the function. Root is the caster rather than the alarm spell.
Shared dream communication requires willing sleep and provides no torment.
The spell enables willing shared dream conversation, without tormenting a sleeper.
Zeah contains Modify Memory, but her prepared entry only supplies ranks0–2 and no preparation of this rank4 spell; possession does not establish usable erasure.

Modify Memory is embedded but the prepared casting entry has only rank 1 and 2 slots and no preparation for this rank 4 spell. This is related spellbook context without established practical erasure access.
A concealed shaft falling trap supplies no chasm-flight ability or relevant crossing method.
A floor trap drops walkers down a chute; it offers no flight or chasm-crossing capability.
Chasm hazard causes a fall and offers a ledge or climb, not flight.
The floor causes a damaging fall into a chasm, opposing safe flight across it.

adjudication.rationale: The hazard is substantively about a chasm and includes a revealed traversable ledge plus climbing/edge-grabbing responses. Its collapse causes a damaging fall, not flight across the chasm. The source triggers on entering a floor section and does not remove flight or force an already flying creature down, so it does not establish an opposite to the requested flying capability.

opinions.rationale: Provides holding-breath and suffocation rules, not ability to breathe water.
The GM screen explains holding breath and drowning, rather than granting underwater breathing.
A stone-themed dragon can turn itself into stone, but that differs from petrifying people.
The dragon manipulates stone and can turn itself into stone, but the relevant abilities do not turn other people to stone.
Creature can collapse ground and structures with innate Earthquake.
Creates an animated shadow illusion rather than an actual living shadow entity.
Rhu-Chalik has innate Rewrite Memory, useful indirect memory-erasure capability; transmitting memories alone copies rather than erases.

Qualified way to keep an enemy still: already grabbed/restrained target becomes unconscious on a critical success. Ordinary success only causes clumsy, so this is less reliable than a direct restraint technique.
A qualified control technique that renders an already grabbed/restrained target unconscious on critical success; normal success only makes it clumsy.
A mutable masked fey supplies qualified masked-spirit flavor without explicit spirit identity.
The lich has fire-related protection content, but Fire Shield makes the shield immune to fire, not the lich; Resist Energy grants resistance.
Fire Shield gives its shield fire immunity and Resist Energy only resistance; neither establishes creature fire immunity.
Floor pressure triggers a ceiling collapse, related collapse hazard content but the floor does not collapse.
Direct healing creature: naga has Heal in a spontaneous repertoire with available slots and can target willing living allies.
Creature can erase memory using linked innate Modify Memory.
Mother Forsythe has Alarm prepared and can choose a mental alert, a useful indirect silent-alarm source.
Fungal curse inflicts pain and hallucinations but no dreams.
The fungal curse impedes movement and inflicts conditions, without dream torment.

Qualified fire immunity through Mist Escape: at 0 HP in escape mist form the vampire is unaffected by further damage, including fire. It is not generally fire immune while active; Fire Shield itself only grants its shield immunity.
The vampire is unaffected by further damage only while at 0 HP in Mist Escape form, a narrow qualified immunity that includes fire; Fire Shield immunity belongs to the shield itself.
Actual sealed room trap floods to ceiling and threatens occupants.
The hazard seals and fills the room to the ceiling with river water.
Useful qualified drowning-location hazard: pool compels victims into water and encircles them to drown; it is a pool rather than an entire flooding room.
The pit causes damaging falls and subsequent drowning, opposing safe downward travel.
The trap actively makes a creature fall and take falling damage, opposing safe descent rather than providing it.
A torture spell is substantively related to torment, but it batters organs directly and supplies no dream intrusion.
The spell inflicts torturous physical pain but has no dream mechanism; related torment content does not fulfill dream torment.
Useful indirect controlled descent: this barghest has innate Levitate, which can move a willing target up or down10 feet per action. It is not an emergency falling reaction.
Water glide supports liquid surface travel, not safe descent through air.
Useful indirect tentacle-grabbing source: this exact Arisept variant has Black Tentacles in a spontaneous repertoire.
Arisept can cast Black Tentacles from his spontaneous repertoire, a useful indirect grabbing-tentacles answer.
Suppresses sound but offers no detection or warning mechanism, so cannot by itself supply a silent alarm.
Related mental curse, but distracts and penalizes waking concentration rather than tormenting sleeping dreams.
A distracting mental curse is related mental torment, but it neither enters dreams nor afflicts a sleeping target specifically.
Creature has prepared Magic Passage and can tunnel solid stone.
Dimension Door only reaches visible spaces at rank4, not through opaque walls.
Its fourth-rank Dimension Door requires seeing the destination, so does not provide travel through opaque walls.
Related magical-item creator/keeper, but not a treasure object that is a monster. Crystal wands are separate creations with no monetary value.
Provides silence plus invisibility, related stealth magic, but no alarm or notification mechanism; cannot infer a combined alarm from silence alone.
A strongly fire-themed prepared and innate dragon caster is a useful alternative to a wizard with fire magic, though its identity and tradition are primal dragon.
Brief reactive concealment is related protection but does not create a shelter.
Momentary concealment protects against an attack but does not conjure a shelter.
Preserves and imparts memories, making them infallibly available temporarily, opposing the requested erasure.
The spell preserves and imparts memories, the opposite of erasing their availability for its recipient.
Reactive amusement distraction has no dream or nightmare function.
The magically engineered fungus has fire healing, but is not a wizard or a caster wielding fire magic.
Saving-throw substitution from adjacent allies creates no shelter; shelter in title is figurative.
Direct method of moving through walls of stone/rock, with once-hourly use and normal stride limits.
Satyr can make enemies unconscious with linked heightened Sleep and pipes.
Grabbles can personally speak with arthropods at will, useful indirect animal communication with a taxonomic restriction.
Grabbles has at-will animal speech limited to arthropods, useful indirect creature access with restricted animals and personal recipient.
Kerinza can permanently petrify a slowed victim with Focus Gaze, directly satisfying the monster capability.
Changes a spell’s origin to a familiar without supplying any shelter spell or shelter construction.
Nathatel receives void healing but its full offensive spell list supplies no means to heal undead.
Alarm directly offers a mental alert for a silent warning.
The spell directly wards an area and sends an optional mental alert, satisfying a silent alarm.
Actual creature has venomous beak and explicit Toxic Bite.
Innate Dive and Breach supplies qualified short surface-to-surface teleport alternative.
Explicitly a faceless undead spirit wearing a stone mask, directly matching the requested creature.
Actual healer has usable Soothe for willing allies and multi-patient care.
Related wall construction and possible bridge/stairs, but creates a solid barrier rather than granting passage through an existing wall.
Direct animated shadow creature; the undead shadow theme fits living shadow without requiring biological life.
Artifact manifests a ritual chamber in Harrowheart but provides no portable shelter.
The artifact can manifest a conjuration chamber in Harrowheart, but does not conjure portable shelter for the user.
A cacophonous damaging noise opposes the requested silent outcome and offers no detection mechanism.
A damaging cacophonous blast supplies no intrusion detection or silent alert.

adjudication.rationale: A loud sonic blast is related to sound-based signaling but provides no intrusion detection or scheduled alert. More specifically, it necessarily produces a cacophonous noise and can deafen affected creatures, reversing the explicitly silent output requirement. The opposite flag concerns this actual noisy outcome, not a claim that the spell is an alarm or that it alerts the intended recipient.

opinions.rationale: Imugi can grant Water Breathing to creatures, a useful indirect caster answer.
The amphibious imugi can also cast Water Breathing on others, useful indirect creature access.
Buoyancy in water is related floating but does not provide safe aerial descent.
Hold is in the warrior name; full abilities do not establish holding an enemy still.
Actual medusa permanently petrifies targets with Focus Gaze.
A feat grants temporary Hit Points to allies but is not an identified healing creature.
An unspecified bearer feat grants allies temporary Hit Points; it identifies neither a creature nor actual restored Hit Points.
A generic effect grants fire weakness, opposing fire immunity and supplying no identified creature.
Creates a metal barrier and permits passage only after a section is broken; it does not enable walking through existing walls.
Explicit human wizard has Fireball prepared.
This explicit wizard prepares Fireball.
The giant viper delivers venom through its fangs, directly answering the requested creature.
A mask-dependent casting feat has no spirit entity connection.
A masked spellcaster protection feat has no spirit identity or spirit content to support the combined query.
The explicitly identified wizard has multiple fire spells prepared, directly answering the requested entity.
The full creature and its abilities concern nightmares and mental attacks, without a petrification capability.
Treasure-collecting monster is related, but the manticore is not itself treasure or a treasure disguise; full entries supply ordinary attacks.
Reverse Gravity causes upward falls and later uncontrolled descent; related floating but no safe downward travel.
Related downward movement, but forcibly drags a grappled creature underwater rather than providing safe floating descent.
Actual viper swarm delivers venom through piercing fangs.
The swarm damages enemies with venomous fangs and delivers its poison.
Creates actual traversable wall tunnel with explicit depth and metal limits.
Spirit Naga is a serpentine aberration, not an authored masked spirit. Its name’s spirit word and optional appearance spells do not establish that concept.
A wearable breathing mask supplies no masked spirit entity.
Room haunt pushes victims into a dry fall, not drowning.
Summons an animate dream but the spell itself does not supply dream torment mechanics.
The viper fangs deliver poison, directly satisfying a venomous bite creature.
This haunt throws occupants out of a chamber to fall; it supplies no drowning room or water confinement.
A chamber haunt that shoves victims into a fall, with no drowning or flooding mechanism.
The queen has Cozy Cabin prepared and can conjure shelter; this is an indirect creature answer with the cabin spell limitations.
Stonemaker has a gaze that permanently petrifies victims, directly satisfying the requested monster.
The basilisk variant has actual permanent petrification on repeated failed gaze saves.
Actual flying creature can cross itself, an indirect flight result.
Vulpinal has constant personal animal speech, useful indirect creature context without granting speech to the requester.
Actual unicorn can heal willing living allies using innate Heal twice.
The unicorn has usable innate Heal targeting willing living creatures, allowing it to heal allies.
Stone giant creates and throws boulders; does not petrify people.
Qualified animal communication tool: imitates one animal type’s calls and aids commands/demoralizing. It does not provide full two-way conversation or understanding.
The trap throws excrement and rotten food onto the opener and requires washing the filth off. It usefully soils a victim, but the source does not explicitly specify lasting clothing stains.
The trap coats its victim in foul material requiring washing, a useful soiling-trap alternative; the source does not explicitly establish stains on clothing.
The trap drops sewage and worms onto nearby creatures, a useful clothing-soiling hazard. A persistent stain or dye is not explicitly established.
The trap dumps sewage onto creatures and thus offers qualified clothing-soiling content. It does not explicitly state persistent stains or a clothing-specific rule.
This bear bites with a jaws Strike, but its fully inspected description and abilities identify an ethereal living beast rather than a stuffed bear.
This is a bear with a piercing jaws Strike, but complete root and abilities describe an ethereal living beast rather than a stuffed bear.
This tabard identifies allegiance and improves social impressions; its complete mechanics have no lost-object location or sword-recovery function.
The tabard aids social impressions and identification of allies; it has no locating or sword-recovery function.

Passive Points directly damages creatures that hit this animal with unarmed Strikes, matching harmful retaliation to punching. The source includes an editorially supplied DC, which does not obscure the behavior.
Passive Points directly damages a creature hitting the porcupine with an unarmed Strike, satisfying the punch-triggered harm request.
Detects poison in an object and can identify its types, but never removes poison from the meal.
Detecting whether food is poisoned is substantively related to meal poisoning, but this spell detects rather than removes poison.
The canine has strong solar/lunar lore, making it related to celestial dogs, but the source describes pursuing sun and moon rather than watching stars.
The canine has substantive celestial sun-and-moon lore, but that lore concerns trying to steal them rather than dogs watching the stars.
This azarketi ancestry feature explicitly grants a base swim Speed of 30, directly satisfying the requested function with its stated ancestry context.
The ancestry feature directly grants a 30-foot swim Speed.
The root identifies an animated skeletal horse, directly a horse monster without skin; the query does not require living exposed flesh.
The source identifies an animated skeletal horse, useful skinless equine monster content, with the qualification that it has a skeletal rather than flayed fleshy appearance.
A moose is a deer that eats leaves and woody matter, substantively related to the deer/plant-eating concept, but the full source does not connect it to eating leshys.

Moose are explicitly deer that eat leaves and woody plants, substantive herbivorous-deer context. Neither full root nor embedded mechanics describe eating leshies, so the combined behavior is not established.
An amphibious sea-devil humanoid with jaws, claws and shark communication is not an alien jellyfish; no substantive jellyfish identity is supplied.
This amphibious humanoid sea devil is a trident-wielding shark communicator, not a friendly alien jellyfish. Root and all embedded abilities were inspected.
Foroxicks directly uses Avenging Bite against a creature within jaws reach that attacks an ally.
Directly meets the requested creature behavior: Avenging Bite reacts to an attack on an ally with a jaws Strike against the attacker, within reach.
This powered machinery hazard hurls metal parts, making it related to a dangerous engine, but its full root and entries attribute motion to overwound springs, not possession.
This is dangerous powered machinery, but the full root and embedded mechanics establish overwound springs and a mechanical trigger, without possession.
This banquet directly produces dissatisfaction even on a critical success, with repeated tasting compelled on a critical failure; it is a direct hazardous never-satisfying banquet.
The banquet explicitly makes every taster unsatisfied, and failed saves create ongoing dissatisfaction or compel another taste. It directly matches the requested hazard.
Zerryd owns Trap Finder with a taken class slot; its explicit checks without Searching supply a useful character example of the method rather than the standalone feat.
Zerryd owns Trap Finder, explicitly allowing checks for traps without Searching. The character sheet is a useful indirect reference to that feat and still requires other detection prerequisites.
The hilt hides a compartment found by studying an already-present weapon. It provides no way to locate a lost sword; finding a compartment is a different target.
This modification hides a scroll-sized object inside a weapon hilt. Finding that compartment is not finding a lost sword, and no locating capability is provided.
Id Ooze Acid explicitly damages metal while sparing stone, reversing the requested preservation of metal.
The id ooze has acid, but explicitly damages metal, directly reversing the requested metal-preserving property.

The plasm resembles an ooze and consists of liquid metal, substantively related material context. Full embedded mechanics show bludgeoning, force and magic consumption rather than acid preserving metal.
This metal elemental explicitly resembles an ooze, but its complete root and embedded systems provide no acid, let alone an acid property preserving metal.

The hydra explicitly regrows two heads from an uncauterized severed stump through Hydra Regeneration. Cauterization and successful saves are ordinary limitations. Source head-count inconsistencies do not obscure this capability.
Hooktongue Hydra explicitly regrows severed heads through Hydra Regeneration, unless stumps are cauterized.
Avenging Bite explicitly makes a jaws Strike when a creature within bite reach attacks the warg’s ally.
Avenging Bite explicitly gives the warg a jaws Strike reaction when a creature in bite reach attacks its ally. It directly answers the requested creature capability.
This exact carnival bear is an animal grizzly variant with damaging jaws. Complete root and all six entries describe a living trained bear rather than a stuffed bear.
A living grizzly variant with jaws is bear-and-biting content, but not a stuffed or animated toy bear.

The feat grants liquid-only Cleanse Cuisine and separately improves a poisoned creature saves. The referenced spell definition is not in the assigned source, so whether it removes meal poison, particularly solid food, cannot be established from this source alone.

The feat grants liquid-only Cleanse Cuisine, but the assigned source does not include that spell's poison-removal mechanics. It explicitly gives only a save bonus when applied to blood. Source expansion is needed to judge meal detoxification defensibly.

adjudication.rationale: Useful qualified method: the feat actually grants innate Cleanse Cuisine and the verified spell explicitly removes toxins from food/beverages. The feat restricts casting to liquids, so it can cleanse a liquid meal or a meal beverage but cannot establish detoxification of an arbitrary solid meal. Its separate blood-purification mode only bonuses ongoing poison saves and does not remove poison from a meal.

opinions.rationale: Swordkeepers guard and store a weapon and project copies of it. That is substantive sword custody context, but the full abilities provide no means to locate a lost sword.
Swordkeepers store and defend weapons, a substantive sword-security connection, but full root and embedded mechanics provide no way to locate a lost sword.
The mutant has a reaction bite, but its trigger is a critical hit against itself, not an attack against an ally.
The mutant has a reactive bite, but its trigger is being critically hit itself, not an ally being attacked. This is substantively related with the wrong protected recipient.
Extract Poison explicitly siphons poison from an object, including wine, and negates its toxicity on a successful counteract. Its weapon transfer and counteract check are ordinary operating limits.
The spell directly counteracts poison on or in an object, explicitly including poisoned wine, and negates its toxicity while transferring the poison to a held weapon.
A pressure-plate blade trap dealing slashing damage; full root and sole reaction provide no clothing staining. Related trap only.
The complete trap cuts creatures with silver blades; it contains no dye, staining, or garment-soiling property. Generic injury does not imply the requested trap concept.

The trap sprays cleaning chemicals and caustic vapor, related liquid-spray hazard content, but its complete mechanics damage and blind creatures rather than stain their clothing. Cleaning as a name is not proof of an opposite stain-removal effect.
The trap sprays solvents and detergents onto a creature, a related chemical-spray hazard, but its complete effects cause acid damage and visual conditions without a clothing stain.
The source provides substantive kholo religious context but identifies a kholo divine conduit, not gremlins worshipping kholos.
This supplies a kholo religious figure, one participant category, but neither the root lore nor relevant abilities identify gremlins worshipping kholos.

The soldier uses a spike launcher made from a manticore tail and has explicit ranged strikes. It is qualified useful tail-spike shooting via a harvested-tail firearm, rather than spikes from the soldier’s own tail.

The Tengu soldier actually fires a spike launcher made from a manticore tail, with Snap Shot and Quick Spiker documenting use. This is qualified tail-spike shooting content, though the tail is a manufactured weapon rather than the soldier own anatomy.
This exact ordinary riding-dog source supplies the dog aspect, but its full root and previously inspected attacks offer no celestial watching characterization.
An ordinary riding dog has no authored star-watching or celestial connection. Shared dog identity alone does not fulfill the phrase.
Nightmare is a monstrous horse, but complete root and embedded entries establish flames and smoke rather than a skinless body.
The source is a flaming equine monster, but the complete record does not establish a skinless horse.
Stargazer is substantive astronomy and sky-observation content, but the background identifies no dogs satisfying the query.
This background substantively concerns astronomical observation, but it does not identify dogs that watch stars. Granting the background to an imagined dog would require unsupported combination.
A bear-themed claw-and-grab feat, but neither a stuffed-bear entity nor a bite ability. Related bear combat content is incomplete.
This bear-themed claw-and-grab feat is related to bear attacks, but supplies no stuffed bear and no bite.
Careful Explorer explicitly grants trap checks without Searching in exploration mode, subject to other trap requirements.
The feat explicitly grants trap-finding checks even without Searching during exploration, directly matching the requested ability.

Zorek has Lock that secures doors, the reverse of opening them. His tomb-specific teleport bypasses space, and Dispel Magic affects magical effects only; neither establishes opening a generally locked door.

The embedded Lock spell fortifies a latch and defeats its normal key, opposite general unlocking; reopening the casters own effect cannot bypass additional locks. Dimension Door supplies related bypass travel in Armag's Tomb, rather than opening an existing door.

This clockwork construct explicitly contains an infesting spirit that can attach fragments of itself to victims. It is useful possessed-machinery content, although a heap of clockwork is not specifically an engine.
The clockwork construct explicitly contains an infesting spirit, a useful possessed-machinery answer. The source identifies a heap of clockwork debris rather than a specific engine.
This is a cooking-contest feast ritual, but successful results explicitly please patrons; an unsuccessful dish is contingent, not a banquet that never satisfies.
A competitive magical feast can disappoint patrons on failure, related banquet dissatisfaction, but neither its successes nor failures create hunger that food cannot satisfy.
The hydra explicitly regrows severed heads using regeneration, unless acid or fire cauterizes the stumps. Ordinary prevention conditions do not weaken the direct match.
Hydra explicitly regrows severed heads through regeneration, with cauterization preventing it; those ordinary limits do not reduce the direct match.
Spiritual Aid rerolls a saving throw. Its complete source identifies no dog or star-watching behavior; the publication title does not supply that entity.
Spiritual Aid rerolls a failed save; its publication mentions stars, but its source identifies no dogs or star-watching function.
This is a dangerous food-preparation hazard with burning splatter and ruined food, but does not describe a banquet that fails to satisfy hunger.
A food-preparation hazard that destroys food and sickens failed cooks is related to dangerous meals, but it is not a banquet that leaves eaters forever unsatisfied.
Giant Pangolin explicitly emits repulsive musk that causes Sickened on failed Fortitude saves. This directly identifies the requested animal without requiring a literal action named Spray.
The animal explicitly emits repulsive musk that sickens nearby creatures. The short emanation is a direct delivery mechanism for the requested sickening musk.
Water Breathing helps underwater survival but its complete mechanics grant breathing, not a swim Speed.
Water Breathing supports underwater survival, but its full mechanics only permit breathing and never grant a swim Speed.
An acid-damaging ooze with metal-sensing and metal-shell abilities, but full root and all six entries do not establish acid that spares metal. Related ooze missing the requested material property.
This ooze deals acid damage and manipulates precious metal, but its complete root and abilities do not establish that its acid leaves metal intact.
Cleansing Flames counteracts poison affecting a creature, but its target is one creature; it cannot remove poison from a meal.
The flames counteract poison in a creature, related cleansing magic, but cannot remove poison from a meal because they target a creature.
The genie contains a palace stocked for a banquet; the relevant palace, hospitality aura, and wish text do not establish a meal that leaves diners unsatisfied. Banquet context alone is incomplete.
Its associated Planar Palace can supply a banquet, but the quoted food and hospitality do not establish a banquet that fails to satisfy. Related banquet context only.
The exact Sezelrian Warg source has Avenging Bite, directly biting enemies that attack allies within jaw reach.
The assigned warg explicitly bites a creature that attacks an ally within its jaws’ reach.
Gray Ooze is an acid ooze, but its acid explicitly damages metal, reversing the requested metal-preserving property.
Gray Ooze is an acid-bearing ooze but explicitly damages metal, reversing the requested preservation of metal.
Befriending a marine familiar is related to a friendly sea creature, but this feat identifies neither an alien nor a jellyfish creature.
Befriending a sea-creature familiar is related to friendly marine creatures, but it identifies no alien jellyfish entity.
The drug enables remote theft of dreaming bodies, substantive possession context. It supplies no engine or machinery possession.
This drug enables distant body theft, a substantive possession-related concept, but identifies neither an engine nor an engine inhabited by a possessing entity.
Water Conjuration explicitly lets an azarketi cast Create Water daily and choose fresh water, a direct way to conjure water for drinking.
This feat explicitly conjures water through innate Create Water and permits choosing fresh water, directly supplying drinking-water conjuration once daily.
This trap describes detecting and disbelieving its illusion with Perception, but provides no ability to notice traps without Searching.
This is a concealed trap whose Perception check can reveal its illusion; it does not grant a way to notice traps without searching.
Vordakai contains Knock, but its ID is absent from every prepared slot in the associated entry. It is related known-spell context, not an established currently usable opening capability.

Vordakai can cast Knock through his once-daily Drain Oculus exception even though Knock is not listed in prepared slots. It assists opening checks/counteracts Lock rather than guaranteeing every lock opens.

adjudication.rationale: Vordakai is an indirect but usable opening-magic provider. Knock is not among his prepared slots, but his explicit once-daily Drain Oculus exception allows any arcane spell up to sixth level even when unprepared, covering the associated second-rank arcane Knock. Knock assists Athletics/Thievery opening checks and counteracts Lock rather than guaranteeing an arbitrary lock opens.

opinions.rationale: The spell creates hunger no eating can sate, directly related to dissatisfaction at meals, but it targets a living creature and does not supply an actual banquet.
Feast of Ashes explicitly makes no amount of food satisfy a creature, useful unsatisfying-feast magic. Its limitation is that it curses the eater rather than creating a banquet.

adjudication.rationale: Useful qualified cause of an unsatisfying feast: on a failed save, Feast of Ashes afflicts its living target with hunger that no amount of eating can sate for the spell's one-week duration. It curses the eater and causes hunger damage; it does not create a banquet or supply food, which limits its fit to the full phrase.

alternativeGrades.rationale: If the intent is an actual banquet or meal-hazard record with the unsatisfying property, this individual hunger curse supplies only a related mechanism and cannot establish the missing banquet.

opinions.rationale: The Nightmare is explicitly a monstrous equine, but complete root and entries describe flames, smoke and planar travel without establishing skinlessness.
A nightmare is explicitly an equine fiend, related horse-monster content, but its full source and abilities describe flame and smoke without skinlessness.
This monster is a magical tail using a reach Tail Slap and constriction, not a tail-spike shooter; its fully inspected attacks and abilities provide substantive tail-monster context only.
The complete creature has a grabbing melee tail slap and warpwave abilities, not tail-spike projectiles; tail vocabulary alone does not fulfill the requested attack.
The creature consumes doses of poison for combat strength and tolerates toxins, but does not extract poison from a meal or make it safe for others.
The creature eats a drawn dose of poison for personal combat strength, but does not remove poison from an existing meal or make food safe for others.
Bonding Meal shares memories and social familiarity through food. Its complete ritual mechanics have no poison detection or removal; a meal alone is not substantive cleansing capability.
This meal ritual shares memories and grants social bonuses; its complete mechanics do not concern poison or food purification. Meal terminology alone does not satisfy the function.
An actual leshy, but full root and its eight entries describe blight and spores rather than deer predation. Supplies one participant only.
The blighted fungus leshy has fungi/spore mechanics and mushroom form, with no deer or deer-predation relationship.
The polar bear has an actual jaws attack and is a bear, but complete source describes a living predator rather than a stuffed bear.
This is a bear with a piercing jaws Strike, but complete root and embedded systems describe a living polar predator rather than a stuffed toy.
Ever-Hunger is a name, not evidence of an unsatisfying banquet. Root and relevant powers describe a xulgath prophet, combat regeneration and life-draining, with no authored feast behavior.

The source has life-devouring magic and a monstrous Ever-Hunger identity, related supernatural consumption, but no banquet or persistent unsatisfied-meal mechanic in the root and relevant special entries.
This is an ooze but its full root and six entries describe gunpowder, fire and explosive residue rather than metal-sparing acid. Related creature family only.

The ooze consumes organic matter, a substantive relation to selective ooze consumption, but its actual attacks use bludgeoning, fire and explosive residue rather than the requested metal-sparing acid.
Secret-Keeper has Locate actually prepared, with mechanics expressly locating a specific sword. Useful indirect means in a creature sheet; range and barriers still apply.
Secret-Keeper has Locate prepared, useful indirect lost-sword finding within 500 feet for an observed object, subject to lead/running-water limits.
A sword concealed in a cane is not a means of locating a lost sword. Full system offers weapon mechanics without locating magic.
The source is a concealed sword, with no lost-object detection or recovery mechanism in its complete text and rules.
The queen has actual Astronomy Lore, a substantive celestial-study connection, but the root and shape-changing mechanics identify a nymph/humanoid rather than dogs watching the stars.
The queen has substantive Astronomy Lore expertise, related to stars, but the root is a nymph and its Change Shape gives humanoid forms, not an identified star-watching dog.
This ooze can randomly spit acid, but its complete root and four entries do not establish selective acid that leaves metal intact.
Amalgam Ooze can spew acid among other liquids, but the complete source has no rule establishing that this acid leaves metal intact. It matches only ooze/acid portions.
A treasure bone with lost scriptures and no mechanics; the word lost is coincidental and provides no sword-finding method.
A saint relic with an empty description has no supplied object-finding capability; lost in its name does not establish relevance to recovering a sword.
Bul-gaes are cosmic canines whose shadow master watches the universe through their distorted light, directly matching the star-watching-dog theme through explicit lore.

The canine lore explicitly describes hounds used to watch the universe through their distorted light. This directly matches the star-watching dog concept without requiring a literal mechanical stargazing action.
The source identifies a predatory flytrap plant, not a skinless horse; sharing general monster status does not establish relevance.
This is a foliage-camouflaged carnivorous plant, not a skinless horse monster.
The rust ooze damages metal weapons with acid and ignores their Hardness, actively reversing the requested metal-preserving outcome.
This is an ooze whose acid actively damages metal weapons and worn/held metal items, reversing the requested outcome of leaving metal intact.
This mundane concealed sword has no locating function; a sword noun alone does not answer finding a lost sword.
This is an ordinary sword concealed inside a cane. Its complete system provides no means of locating a lost sword; sharing the sword noun does not provide the requested function.
Hiding among crowds and disguise feats do not detect traps or permit passive trap finding.
Hiding among crowds and gaining disguise feats does not provide passive trap detection.
Verdurous Ooze explicitly has acid that damages metal and corrodes metal weapons. It is related ooze/acid content that reverses the requested preservation of metal.

The creature intrinsically conjures a decadent feast with no nutritional substance, directly supplying a banquet that fails to nourish. It also manipulates those who eat it.
The feat deciphers briefly seen or sealed writing. Its full text has no passive trap-noticing function; the notice wording concerns witnesses noticing the reader.
The feat deciphers writing from glimpses and sealed letters. Noticing witnesses is incidental vocabulary; it provides no passive trap detection.
The blood-draining trap manifests blood as airborne mist, a substantive soiling-adjacent connection, but it does not say it stains clothing.
The trap creates bloody mist, substantively related to soiling, but specifies blood drain and void damage rather than staining clothing.
Feet to Fins directly grants a swim Speed; its reduced land Speed is an explicit normal tradeoff rather than failure to grant the requested movement.
The spell directly grants a willing creature a swim Speed equal to its normal land Speed. The reduced land Speed is an explicit ordinary tradeoff.
Knock directly helps open a locked door, grants a +4 bonus, permits a Thievery check during casting and counteracts Lock. Its ordinary skill check does not make it indirect.
Knock directly makes a locked door easier to open, allows an opening check during casting, and counteracts Lock. Needing a check is an ordinary operating limit.
This anti-lockpicking trap paralyzes and hurts the picker, but the full root and reaction do not break lockpicks.
This trap responds to lockpicking, making it substantively relevant, but it injures and paralyzes the picker rather than breaking lockpicks.
Quick Swim explicitly grants a swim Speed at legendary Athletics; that rank condition is stated rather than omitted.
Quick Swim explicitly grants a swim Speed when legendary in Athletics, directly meeting the function. At lower proficiency it improves Swim distance only; that qualification is explicit.

This dragon has an actually associated at-will Create Water spell that produces drinkable water, useful indirect capability content in a creature sheet. Desert Thirst can destroy liquid instead, but does not require replacement of creation.

The dragon has associated at-will Create Water, explicitly making drinkable water. Desert Thirst optionally destroys liquid instead, so destruction is not mandatory. The creature is an indirect spell reference.
Kanker is a ghast alchemist with toxin and ritual mechanics, not a possessed engine. His complete root and relevant ritual/unique entries supply no machinery possession relationship.
This ghast alchemist carries Midnight Milk, whose lore concerns stealing dreaming bodies. That is substantive indirect possession context, but the identified root is a ghast, not a possessed engine.
The feat modifies animal-inspired unarmed attacks, but identifies no animal that damages someone for punching it.
The feat improves an animal-instinct barbarian unarmed attack; it neither identifies an animal nor damages an attacker when punched.
The creature uses a bludgeoning melee tail attack with knockdown; its complete source has no spikes or tail projectiles. A tail noun alone does not meet the specialized attack concept.
The centipede has an effective tail melee attack, but the complete entries establish bludgeoning reach and knockdown rather than shooting tail spikes.
The feat uses watery transformation for translocation, with no conjured drinkable water in its complete prose or rules. Shared water terminology is coincidental to the requested supply function.
The feat uses a water-like body transformation to teleport; it supplies no drinking water. Shared water vocabulary does not fulfill conjuring a drink.
Avenging Bite explicitly reacts to an ally being attacked with a jaws Strike against the attacker within reach.
Avenging Bite directly makes a jaws Strike against a creature attacking a warg ally within reach.

The undead dog has a harmful nearby stench and attacks, but complete root and four entries do not make being punched trigger harm; the aura is proximity based. It is related dangerous-animal content without the requested retaliation.
The undead hound has a harmful stench and biting attacks, but its full entries provide no harm triggered by punching it; former-owner bonus damage is a different condition.
The complete haunt concerns a relic and mind control near stairs, not a banquet or unsatisfied diners. Hunger is an artifact name, not the requested meal behavior.
The haunt attacks with void energy and compels dropping a relic. Hunger is part of a relic name, without a banquet or unsatisfied eating mechanic.
The barded manticore directly flings tail spikes as ranged attacks.
The manticore explicitly flings spikes from its tail with ranged Strikes, directly matching the requested monster capability.
The effect enhances animal-inspired unarmed attacks, related to animal combat but identifying no animal that hurts someone for punching it.
The effect modifies a bestial-rage unarmed attack, related animalistic combat content, but supplies no animal that retaliates against punches.
The source is a wolf-like warg with jaws attacks, not an animated stuffed bear; biting alone is too generic to establish the requested concept.
The warg is a speaking wolf-like beast with jaws, not a stuffed bear. A generic bite does not establish the requested combined identity.

The ooze lore includes insatiable appetites and dissolving objects, related endless consumption rather than a banquet that fails to satisfy diners. Root and relevant powers describe acid combat, not that meal.
Insatiable ooze appetites relate to never being satisfied, but this corrosive creature is not a banquet or a food effect.
The summoned turtle has a swim Speed and transports passengers, but the caster/passengers do not gain a swim Speed. Related water travel with a different recipient.
The spell conjures a swimming mount and boat-like transport; it does not grant the user a swim Speed. Related water travel falls short of the stated capability.
The source is a horse but describes a normal domesticated mount, with full embedded abilities providing no skinless monster characterization.
War Horse supplies the horse entity, but complete root and all three entries describe an ordinary mount rather than a skinless monster.
Avenging Bite explicitly makes a jaws Strike when a creature within reach attacks the dire warg’s ally.
The exact variant has Avenging Bite: it reacts with a jaws Strike when a creature in reach attacks one of its allies.
The root describes a horrifying horse/scorpion demon and its form-changing ability, so it is related horse-monster content, but skinless appearance is not established.
The source describes a horse-scorpion demon, related to the horse-monster request, but neither root nor its full embedded descriptions establish skinlessness.
The spyglass is expressly used for watching stars, but it is equipment and supplies no dogs satisfying the requested entity.
This spyglass is substantively about watching stars, but does not identify any dogs with that behavior; hypothetical use by a dog is unsupported.
This magic imprisons a target behind additional locked doors and suppresses escape, reversing the requested opening/access outcome.
This spell creates locked barriers and traps a creature behind them, reversing the desired opening of a locked door for passage.
The prison form actively prevents a creature leaving a confined structure or damaging it to escape, opposing the requested opening for passage. It is related barrier magic, not unlocking.
The ritual concerns magical confinement and prevention of escape, a related barrier/traversal concept, but does not open an existing locked door. Its target is a creature rather than a door.

adjudication.rationale: Related confinement/barrier magic, but the ritual imprisons a creature rather than opening an existing locked door. Its Prison form prevents the target leaving or damaging a confined area; ending this confinement is described separately. That opposes an escape goal, but the actual query asks to open a door, and the source does not itself shut, lock or strengthen a door. I therefore do not infer the opposite flag from a broader escape intention.

opinions.rationale: This werebear feat grabs with claw Strikes. It is related bear combat content, but identifies neither a stuffed bear nor a biting one.
A werebear claw-and-grab feat does not describe a stuffed toy or a bite; the bear word alone does not establish this requested entity.

Tiger is a dangerous animal with offensive jaws, claws and wrestling, but all root and embedded mechanics show no harm triggered by being punched. General predation is related but does not meet retaliation intent.
The tiger has pounce, sneak attack, wrestling and grabbing, but no authored damage response to being punched. Being a dangerous animal alone is insufficient.
This meaningfully provides a swim Speed of 25, but only by improving the Water Nagaji prerequisite swim Speed rather than granting swimming to someone without it.
This upgrades an existing swim Speed from 10 to 25 feet. It usefully supplies a better swim Speed but requires already being a Water Nagaji, rather than granting initial swimming capability.
This dock worker has a water-breathing potion, which changes breathing after drinking; neither that item nor the other actions conjures drinking water.
This dock worker has a water-breathing potion and fishing abilities. Neither those mechanics nor its other fully inspected equipment conjures drinking water.

Marcien has Lock associated with his spontaneous casting entry. Its effect secures a latch against others rather than opening an existing locked door; the caster-only reopening exception applies only to his own magic and no additional lock.

The embedded Lock spell fortifies a latch and invalidates its key, opposing opening an existing locked door. Its caster can reopen their own magical lock only if no other bar or lock exists; this is not general unlocking magic. All other embedded spell descriptions and abilities were inspected.
This is substantively a dog creature, but its complete root and abilities describe a mundane loyal mount with no star-watching association.
An ordinary loyal riding dog meets only the dog part of this concept; its full root and three abilities supply no star-watching characterization.
The amoeba is an amelekana minion, giving related context to that alien creature, but the returned root is a mindless amoeba rather than a friendly alien jellyfish.
The amoeba is an aquatic, semi-independent minion of an amelekana, related gelatinous companion content, but the source establishes neither a jellyfish identity nor friendly alien character.
Counteracts poison afflicting a willing creature after dealing a little poison damage. It addresses poisoning in a patient rather than removing poison from food.
This counteracts poison afflicting a willing creature, with a small poison-damage cost, but cannot purify a meal because its target is a creature.
This anti-entry trap damages and paralyzes a creature opening without a key, but the full root and reaction do not damage lockpicks.
This door rune triggers on opening without the key, related lock-intrusion defense, but full mechanics injure and paralyze the intruder rather than break lockpicks.
A taxidermy Sandpoint Devil trap exhales smoke; full root and reaction have no deer eating leshys.
A taxidermy Sandpoint Devil emits enfeebling smoke; it is unrelated to deer eating leshies.
Guarded Thoughts blocks attempts to obtain thoughts: failed counteracting yields no information, reversing the requested mind-reading outcome for the reader.
This feat blocks others from obtaining the bearer's thoughts, directly opposing the requested thought-reading outcome unless counteracted.

An animal that reacts with a damaging Strike when attacked within reach while Feigning Death. Punching it under that authored trigger provokes retaliation; the death-feigning state is an ordinary operating condition.
This animal can Strike the creature that attacks it while Feigning Death, directly providing retaliation when punched under that stated trigger.
Mind Reading directly reveals surface thoughts on a failed Will save, with repeated readings on a critical failure. Save and temporary immunity are ordinary limitations.
The spell directly reads surface thoughts on a failed target save; ordinary saving throw limits do not make the answer indirect.
Opens a specific interplanetary portal at standing stones, related magical doorway content, but it cannot unlock an ordinary existing door.
This ritual magically opens a specific interplanetary portal, a related doorway/traversal concept, but does not unlock an existing locked door.
The hazard has a mental fear/suggestion effect and no staining mechanic in its complete root or reaction. It matches only the trap portion; filth merely hides its rune.
This trap frightens and mentally harms intruders, forcing them out of the room. Its root and full reaction contain no dye or clothing-staining effect.
Toxic Body directly hurts an unarmed attacker with spines and venom after a failed Reflex save, exactly matching an animal that hurts someone who punches it.
The animal Toxic Body directly harms melee unarmed attackers with piercing spines and venom, fulfilling the punched-animal request.
The animal exposes creatures that hit it with unarmed attacks to goblin pox, which inflicts sickened and slowed conditions. This directly supplies harmful retaliation to punching.
This animal exposes an unarmed attacker to goblin pox, whose stages sicken and slow the attacker; it directly penalizes punching the animal.
After reading all attacks and abilities, this sea devil uses manufactured lance/spear attacks, claws and jaws, with no tail-spike shooting. A spear metal spike is incidental vocabulary.
This sea devil attacks with a lance, claws, jaws and a thrown spear. Full embedded mechanics show no tail-spike mechanism; a spear spike is equipment, not a tail capability.
An actual trap whose fluid walls knock down and bludgeon victims. Full root and both entries have no clothing-staining effect.
The hall softens its walls to knock down and bludgeon creatures. Complete root and both embedded entries provide no clothing, dye or staining effect; merely being a trap is insufficient.
An actual magical engine that creates an owb defender, but creation is not possession by that creature. Full root and sole reaction establish dangerous machinery without an animating possessor.

The engine creates an owb prophet from shadows, a meaningful supernatural engine relationship. The source identifies the prophet as its creation rather than a possessing entity, leaving the possession request unmet.
The unguent is substantively related foul-smelling musk, but it conceals wearers from fungi and identifies no animal that sprays sickening musk.
This foul-smelling musk is an applied alchemical camouflage against fungi. It is substantively scent-related but supplies neither an animal nor a sickening spray.

The inspected Kashrishi page establishes empathy and explicitly cautions against mistaking it for thought reading. The multi-ancestry journal may contain other relevant pages; without completing those pages I cannot defensibly resolve the root record’s usefulness.

The ancestry journal discusses psychic empathy, including people mistaking Kashrishi empathy for thought reading. Its specified sense reads vague emotions rather than specific thoughts, so it is related but does not deliver the function.

adjudication.rationale: The ancestry journal gives substantive psychic-empathy context, especially Kashrishi, but does not establish the requested thought-reading function. Although its introductory flavor mentions neighbors' thoughts, its dedicated explanation calls apparent thought reading a misunderstanding and its actual sense provides vague emotions without specific details. The full Kashrishi, Conrasu and Poppet pages and all-page thought/psychic/empathy navigation do not supply a demonstrated method for reading someone's thoughts.

opinions.rationale: This hatch curse deals force damage and worsens saves, with no meal or banquet relationship in the complete hazard.
This hatch trap curses trespassers with force damage and penalties. Its complete source has no feast, food, or unsatisfied hunger.
This weapon rune grants unholy damage, not a possessed engine or a machinery possession effect.
A fiendish weapon rune supplies extra spirit damage and bleed; it identifies no possessed engine or engine-possession mechanism.
The tomb raider’s Hazard Spotter explicitly grants trap checks without Searching. The creature is a useful indirect example of the requested ability.
Tomb Raider explicitly gets trap-finding checks without Searching via Hazard Spotter, a useful indirect NPC example of the requested function.
The haunt explicitly animates an alchemical engine with a spirit that must be ejected from its shell, directly matching a possessed engine.
An animating spirit inhabits an alchemical engine and can be ejected from its mechanical shell. This directly fulfills possessed engine.
This is a faceless masked ghost with a body of mist, rather than an equine creature. Peeling faces is not a skinless horse identity.
The source identifies a faceless masked humanoid spirit rather than a skinless horse; a lack of a face does not establish the requested combined entity.
The manticore explicitly fires tail spikes, including a Spike Volley attack and a limit of twelve spikes per day. It directly identifies the requested monster.
The manticore directly flings tail spikes with its ranged Spike and Spike Volley mechanics.
The undead relives starvation and transmits its agony, a substantive hunger theme; it supplies no banquet or food that fails to satisfy. All seven embedded entries were inspected.
Starvation and hallucinations provide a substantive hunger-related connection, but this undead has no banquet or food that fails to satisfy in its complete source.
A supernatural feast in which spirits eat victims, not a banquet offered to diners that fails to satisfy. The devouring connection is substantive but the recipient and outcome differ.
Cannibalistic Echoes is a feeding-themed haunt whose spirits devour nearby living creatures. It has no banquet or unsatisfying-food effect in its complete root and sole Feast action.
The banquet explicitly leaves tasters unsatisfied and compulsively tasting more, directly matching the described hazard.
This banquet repeatedly dissatisfies tasters and can compel another taste, directly matching the description.
Assisting Shot is a ranged Strike that helps a later attacker; neither its name nor mechanics supply a plausible completion of assur.
Assisting Shot grants an ally an attack bonus after a ranged hit; neither its identity nor mechanics plausibly completes assur.
This is an actual clockwork creature, with wind-up operation and clockwork mechanisms.
A domesticated guard and diving hound is substantively related to dogs, but its full aquatic hunting lore and abilities do not establish watching the stars.
These are diving hunting and guard dogs, substantively canine but with no source-supported star-watching connection in root or abilities.
A sovereign imperial dragon selecting rulers is not a source-supported completion of emperor cob; imperial vocabulary alone does not establish the requested subject.
A sovereign dragon involved in selecting mortal rulers does not identify or substantively answer the truncated named emperor cob subject.
Kolo wears studded leather armor, which is substantive possession context but does not make this creature a useful answer to the armor lookup.
A concealed trap with expert detection details is related to trap detection, but its attacks and conditions do not grant noticing traps without searching.
A concealed rope trap has detection DC and disable mechanics, but grants no way to notice traps without Searching.
A divine beam causing spirit damage has a substantive spiritual attack relationship, but does not conjure an armament or provide a close source-supported weapon variant.
A divine spirit-damage beam is thematically related spiritual attack magic, but supplies no manifested armament and is not a plausible name completion.
The animal exposes anyone hitting it with an unarmed attack to a disease causing sickened and slowed conditions, directly answering the harmful-contact request.
An animal whose dander exposes an unarmed attacker to debilitating disease directly matches being harmed when punched; harm need not be hit point damage.
This creature includes a prepared Spiritual Weapon, substantive context for the truncated spell name, but incidental spell ownership does not answer the requested spell subject usefully.
Sepoko prepares Spiritual Weapon, related manifested-weapon magic, but the root is a cleric rather than a spell completion for spiritual arma. No verified alias establishes identity.
This is a polymorph trap that transforms trespassers into aeons; the axiomatic variant directly fits the unqualified polymorph-trap request.
This is directly a polymorph trap: its glyph transforms trespassers into aeons.
This bard includes Dream Message, a related communication spell, rather than being a record about Sending; the creature context adds no source-backed answer to the spell lookup.
The bard has Dream Message, a related one-way communication spell delayed until sleep; this NPC is not a useful alternative spell record to Sending.
An actual craftable alarm snare is a direct instance of the requested broad category.
A particular functional snare directly answers the unfiltered snare category.
Redirecting expended smite energy to a different target is substantively related to a rebounding attack, but this reaction provides no thrown-weapon toss or useful close variant of it.
The hazard channels magma through lava spouts into a maze and attacks with gouts, directly fitting a lava-flume hazard concept despite its different title.
A lava-spewing mechanical maze trap is a useful related hazard; its explicit mechanism is targeted spouts rather than a lava flume.
The exact Hidden Pit hazard supplies the concealed trapdoor and pit mechanics requested.
A useful companion spell explicitly casts Ignition and improves its action cost, but is a higher-rank focus spell rather than Ignition itself.

This hireable mage has an actually prepared Knock that aids opening locks and permits a Thievery check during casting. It is a useful indirect provider of the requested magic rather than the spell record.
A useful indirect source: this hireable mage has prepared Knock to assist opening a locked door, including the opening check. The returned record is a caster rather than the magic itself.
The golem has an intrinsic superheated-steam vent attack, a useful related implementation of steam vents; the root is a creature rather than a dedicated vent hazard.
Useful steam-venting creature ability: the golem emits superheated steam from its forge. This is an attack on a creature root, rather than an environmental vent feature.
The exact Hidden Pit record directly answers this unfiltered hazard name lookup.
Exact requested hazard.
A communal cockroach with mandibles and scurrying is not a source-supported slug variant; sharing giant-animal scale is insufficient.
A giant cockroach shares only the broad animal category; its colony ecology does not establish a slug or a close slug variant.
The guard dog has jaws and ally-based Pack Attack damage, but no reaction to an ally being attacked; its full two-entry combat set does not provide the requested bite trigger.
The dog has a bite and ally-based bonus damage, but its complete abilities provide no reaction to an ally being attacked.
Cooling objects and creating nonmagical ice directly answers broad frost spell discovery. The gelid-shard context and minor effects are ordinary spell qualifications.
An animated book and origami locust swarm neither supplies deer nor a leshy-eating event. Its creature-targeted paper cuts do not establish the requested hazard concept.
An enchanted book becomes cutting origami locusts; this is not a deer or a leshy-eating encounter.

An extraplanar jellyfish-shaped elemental is substantively related, but its lore establishes elusive schools rather than friendliness, and its attack can drown targets. The requested friendly characterization is unsupported.
An extraplanar jellyfish-like elemental fits part of the image, but its source provides no friendliness and describes an attack that drowns targets.
This hazard explicitly unleashes a channel of lava that sweeps creatures away, directly fitting lava-flume discovery even though it also produces other disasters.
The hazard includes a flowing Lava Channel that sweeps creatures away, useful for a lava-flume hazard, but this is one option among several natural disasters.
The exact Sending spell directly answers the name lookup.
Exact requested spell.

The patroller has explicit rapid daily snare-crafting mechanics and named snare options, making this a useful indirect snare-user resource beyond mere kit possession. The root is a creature rather than a snare.
This magical banquet is substantively about unusual undead hunger, but it explicitly sates its undead diners for 24 hours, reversing the unsatisfying-banquet outcome.
This supernatural banquet is substantively related, but it satisfies undead hunger for 24 hours, reversing the requested unfulfilling property.
The creature includes an innate Wall of Thorns, but this is incidental casting ownership for a spell-subject lookup rather than a dedicated explanation or useful alternative root record.
The creature includes an innate Wall of Thorns spell; this is a substantive spell reference rather than a thorn-wall record or dedicated explanation.
A lava-stream inhabitant that flings nearby magma is substantively related, but neither its lore nor its abilities supplies a lava flume.
Lava-stream habitat and flung magma relate to lava, but an otter is not a lava flume or channel and its abilities do not supply one.
This silver mirror is a direct instance of the requested mirror equipment category; the gilded art-object presentation does not defeat that match.
The creature has a damaging melee tail, but the complete attacks and actions show clobbering rather than firing tail spikes.
A strong melee tail is related tail-based monster offense; it does not shoot spikes.
Splintershank includes a prepared Wall of Thorns, providing substantive spell ownership context rather than a useful root answer to this spell-subject lookup.
The twigjack has a prepared Wall of Thorns spell, but the NPC root is primarily a caster and merely references the requested wall spell.
The drug lore describes remotely stealing bodies, a substantive possession connection, but its experimental effects and lore do not identify or possess an engine.
The drug is tied to stealing dreaming victims’ bodies, related possession lore, but supplies no possessed machine or engine.
The complete trap inflicts enfeeblement, mental damage and fear through shadow breaths; being a trap alone does not relate it to breaking lockpicks.
This trap drains strength and inflicts mental fear attacks. No lockpick-breaking relationship appears in the complete trap mechanics. Trap category alone is insufficient.
Electrical discharges and lightning are substantively storm-related, but this hazard has no thunderclap or sonic effect in its root or sole reaction.
An electricity-discharge hazard is substantively storm-related but lacks a thunderclap or sonic effect.
An ethereal bear that becomes mist is not identified as an owlbear or a source-supported close owlbear variant; shared bear ancestry vocabulary alone is insufficient.

Disk Rider explicitly makes a floating disk into a heavy shield with durability statistics, a meaningful special shield implementation beyond incidental possession. The creature is an indirect result for broad shield discovery.
Grimmnir has a trained Intimidation skill and an actually granted Intimidating Glare, making the character a useful example of silent demoralizing rather than the general feat record.
This character demonstrates the actual solution, Intimidating Glare, which removes the auditory trait; the limitation is that the returned record is a complete character rather than the feat.
A gentle domesticated riding horse has no skinless-monster characterization in its root or complete combat entries. Horse identity alone does not substantively answer the combined concept.
An ordinary riding horse matches the horse component but supplies none of the requested skinless monster characterization in its root or abilities.
The wolf and its victims rise as undead floodslain, substantively related to return from death, but neither ordinary resurrection nor a useful resurrection resource.
Its victims rise as undead, a substantive reanimation connection but not restoration to life or the resurrection ritual.
This dedicated family rule explains mechanical exceptions while prone and improved crawling, useful qualified prone rules content; it does not supply the base condition definition.
This rule is useful for prone combat, explicitly changing prone penalties and crawling, but is a zombie-specific exception rather than the general condition.
Actual self-resurrection as a Resurrect ritual directly supplies broad resurrection subject discovery. Its once-yearly personal limitation is explicit and does not negate the intrinsic topic match.
Useful qualified resurrection example: the tidehawk returns itself to life under water/remains and annual-use restrictions, not a means to resurrect another creature.
The lore explicitly describes a horselike hybrid monstrosity lacking every patch of skin, directly answering the creature concept.
The source explicitly describes a horselike monster whose entire hybrid body lacks skin, directly matching the requested creature.

A source-supported healing consumable alternative, but it requires three actions and heals only 1 HP per minute in a stationary mist instead of immediate minor-potion drinking. Its higher level and wind vulnerability matter.
A healing consumable is a useful functional alternative, but this costly moderate vapor heals slowly over minutes and affects an area rather than acting as a minor potion.
This is an actual golem instance, with root lore and traits directly identifying the category.
The effect directly grants a 20-foot swim Speed for 24 hours and identifies the elixir that supplies it.
Direct effect granting a swim Speed, explicitly linked to its originating elixir.
Avenging Bite explicitly triggers on an attack against an ally within jaws reach and makes a jaws Strike at that attacker. This directly matches the requested creature ability.
Avenging Bite explicitly makes a jaws Strike when a creature in reach attacks a warg ally; this is the requested creature capability.
The dragon has an actually prepared Wall of Thorns, but incidental spell ownership is related context rather than a useful root answer to the spell-subject lookup.
This dragon prepares Wall of Thorns; the root is a spellcasting creature example rather than a completion of the named spell query.
A magical diorama trap firing apocalypse beams has a substantive apocalyptic-hazard theme, but no orb or source-supported equivalence to Armageddon Orb.
An apocalypse-themed diorama beam trap is related destructive doom content, but does not identify an Armageddon Orb or a close orb variant.
The hooked rod trains and commands animals. Its superficially crowbar-like shape does not establish prying use or a useful crowbar alternative.
The bullhook is an animal-command tool with no supported levering or Force Open purpose; its rod shape alone does not make it a crowbar alternative.
This trickster fey avatar is not identified as Armageddon Orb or a related orb hazard; general powerful magic and flame abilities do not establish that subject.
The source describes a capricious fey avatar, not the named orb or a supported alternative to it. General dangerous magic is insufficient.
The verified Sea Devil Brute alias establishes this sedacthy as a direct sea-devil creature-family result. Root lore independently describes its aquatic marauding role.
Direct sea-devil family discovery: artifact-verified alias Sea Devil Brute identifies this sedacthy variant.
A plausible named sustenance spell completion that restores undead vigor via fast healing, directly useful for unqualified sustenance discovery without imposing a food-only intent.
The named sustenance spell directly sustains an undead creature by restoring vigor with fast healing; the broad query imposes no food-only requirement.
The item actively drains opponents life essence to grant its wielder temporary HP, directly answering broad vampiric content discovery.
The weapon directly embodies vampiric life-draining mechanics, converting a foe's damage into temporary health.
This enforcer merely wears studded leather armor. That is related possession context, without a useful root answer to the armor lookup.
The enforcer wears Studded Leather Armor, a related armor variant, but its root remains an incidental wearer.
The spell explicitly offers a swim Speed equal to half normal Speed; choosing that mode directly achieves the requested function.
A spell directly grants a chosen swim Speed. Its focus-spell duration and half-Speed rate are ordinary operating limitations.
Sajan carries a crowbar in a backpack; the character is incidental ownership context rather than the requested item resource.
Sajan carries a crowbar; inventory possession alone gives related context rather than the requested equipment record.
Etward includes Dream Message with special dream invasion, substantive related communication content, but neither the root nor its unique mechanic is about Sending.
Etward has Dream Message and dream-invasion mechanics, related remote communication, but the root is neither Sending nor a direct spell alternative.

The character has an actually granted Plant Nourishment feature explaining sustenance through photosynthesis and minerals, a useful indirect nutrition example. It is a character-specific presentation with sunlight qualifications rather than a general sustenance resource.
Fluff Fang has the standard leshy Plant Nourishment feature, but the character record merely supplies ancestry context for sustenance rather than a dedicated answer.

adjudication.rationale: Useful qualified sustenance example: this leshy character actually receives Plant Nourishment from its ancestry, supplying nourishment through photosynthesis, minerals or decaying matter without ordinarily paying for food. The feature includes sunlight/starvation and bottled-sunlight qualifications. It is an intrinsic nutrition mechanism in a particular character record, not merely carried rations; it does not feed other creatures.

alternativeGrades.rationale: If the one-word query seeks a dedicated sustenance resource or a way to sustain an arbitrary adventurer, this prebuilt leshy is only a character-specific ancestry example. Its personal nourishment cannot be transferred to others.

opinions.rationale: The creature has a specific defense against Grapple, but its slime and combat abilities do not provide the Grapple action or useful grappling instruction.
Fallenta includes associated spontaneous Sending and a Sending wand, but the root remains a bard with incidental spell ownership rather than a useful answer to the spell lookup.
Fallenta has Sending in a spontaneous repertoire, but the NPC is incidental spell ownership rather than the named spell record.
Trip is a directly useful way to impose prone and explains its success/failure outcomes, but it is the causing action rather than the requested condition definition.
Trip is a useful rule for inflicting prone, including success and critical-failure outcomes; it does not explain the condition itself.
Halran is a human duelist with sword abilities and no harrowkin identification in its full root/system or items. A vaguely similar name is not subject evidence.
Halran is a human duelist; complete root and combat abilities do not identify a harrowkin or a related family variant.
The warrior wears Leather Armor, substantive possession context but not a useful armor-subject answer.

A dedicated griffon-predation haunt provides a usable griffon-themed encounter: it reenacts griffons taking a priest to feed their chicks. It is a qualified related result rather than griffon creature statistics.
This haunt presents a detailed griffon predation scene and its encounter effects, useful related material for griffons; it provides an illusory death experience rather than griffon statistics.
The card creates an acting duplicate and alternate-life twins. The verb mirrors does not make it a reflective mirror or substantiate a useful mirror-equipment alternative.
A shadow duplicate that mirrors actions relates to reflection/duplication, but is a card artifact rather than mirror equipment.
Moths feed on blood or scraps to heal the caster and sense rot; no mechanic removes toxins from a meal. A food mention does not establish purification.
The moth spell forages and heals its caster; references to food do not supply any poison removal or purification.
The artifact-backed Magic Missile alias establishes Force Barrage as the exact requested spell identity; the source supplies automatically hitting force shards.
Lini has an actually prepared Ignition, but this is a character with incidental spell ownership rather than a useful answer to the spell-subject lookup.
Trip Snare is an actual specific snare, directly answering broad snare discovery.

The haunt supplies a detailed applied Grapple encounter with checks, restraint and escape stakes, useful indirect rules context. It is a specific drowning haunt rather than the general Grapple action.
Merisiel carries a crowbar in her backpack; possession alone is related context rather than a useful item-lookup result.

adjudication.rationale: Useful poison-specific removal guidance is explicitly provided in the root lore: azarpal-contaminated food or drink can be detoxified with Cleanse Cuisine or one hour of alchemical work using a lab and a Crafting check against its poison DC. The creature's own Gulp or Grab actively laces stored food with poison after 24 hours, so that source-backed behavior reverses the requested removal outcome; the useful answer is the remediation instructions, not using the azarpal to cleanse meals.

The weretiger is animal-shaped and has Reactive Strike, but the assigned source supplies only an unresolved localization token for that reaction. Its trigger cannot be checked here, so whether punching it causes a retaliatory attack remains unproven. Other authored actions do not resolve that trigger.

adjudication.rationale: Related animal-shaped combatant with a reactive attack, but the verified Reactive Strike trigger concerns manipulate/move actions, ranged attacks, and leaving squares during movement. Being punched is not its stated trigger. The complete root and embedded abilities provide no punch-triggered damage or retaliation; ordinary offensive jaws, claws, Rend and Wrestle do not fulfill that conditional function.

opinions.rationale: The augur has associated innate Augury, but the returned creature is incidental caster context rather than the named spell.

The Augur fiend has associated innate Augury twice, so the relation is real, but the creature root is principally a pain-focused velstrac with incidental spell-list inclusion rather than the named spell.
A falling portcullis trap crushes and pins creatures, without affecting lockpicks. Generic trap status alone is insufficient.
The portcullis crushes and pins intruders; it has no lockpick-breaking mechanism. A trap requiring Thievery is insufficient to establish that requested function.
Yoon carries the exact minor healing potion, but the character is incidental owner context for the named item.
Level-1 Yoon carries a minor healing potion; that is incidental inventory rather than a dedicated potion answer.

A dedicated acid-resistance potion directly answers broad acid content discovery. No acid-production requirement is stated, so its protective direction is not contradictory.
A monstrous undead horse with rotting flesh and exposed entrails is a useful close visual alternative, although the source does not explicitly describe it as wholly skinless.

The moldering steed is a horse monster with rotting flesh and exposed entrails, a useful qualified match for an exposed-flesh horse concept. The source does not literally identify a fully skinless horse.

A narrow destruction alternative removes natural difficult terrain by decomposing vegetation. Useful for that obstacle-removal subset, but not the named Disintegrate spell or general matter destruction.

Decompose supplies a specialized destructive alternative that decays plants and destroys natural difficult terrain. It is much narrower than Disintegrate and does not vaporize arbitrary objects or creatures.
